pr_title: Support SET SCHEMA and SET SEARCH_PATH
pr_body:
Please take a look when you have time?
This series of changes fix #155.

I found some interesting things along the way. These can be addressed in separate PR:

 * The "temp" schema is a bit limiting. We might want to support TEMP tables without using this?
 * Using "main" schema for built-ins can be problematic because since these built-ins become invisible after
   setting the search_path. We might give them their own, like "builtin" or something.
 * The queries in CREATE VIEW can break after the search_path change. We might want to either
   pre-compile these queries somehow or retain the search path for the later resolution.

Anyway, these aren't the main points of this PR. 

Also, I credit #1451 where I borrowed the test. Thanks @rohankumar42!
pr_comments: Tried to run SQLancer locally but no luck :-(

Thanks for the review Mark! PTAL?
The update
 * dropped the error message retrieval and "did you mean" handling. I'll send this part as separate PR once this is in.
 * added DEFAULT_SCHEMA back to the search path regardless of the user-set schema.

----
> I'm not opposed to letting temporary tables live in any schema. The main point of the temporary schema is that this is connection-local, so temporary objects from one connection do not interfere with temporary objects from another connection. We could let this be the default for temporary objects, and if the schema is explicitly specified elsewhere store them in that schema.
> 
Oh I didn't think about this. Thanks for the catch!
Although it would be possible to extend schema / catalog entries to be connection-aware, it might be a bit too complicated for its value.

> > Using "main" schema for built-ins can be problematic because since these built-ins become invisible after setting the search_path. We might give them their own, like "builtin" or something.
> 
> The easiest solution would be to always include the "main" schema on the search path (similar to how postgres always includes pg_catalog on the search path). We could consider adding a separate SYSTEM_SCHEMA (e.g. `duckdb`) that holds the built-in functions like pg_catalog.
> 
This would be nice. Then we can drop DEFAULT_SCHEMA from the search path, which I guess what PG does.
But let me leave DEFAULT_SCHEMA in the search path for now. Adding SYSTEM_SCHEMA will be a big change.

> > The queries in CREATE VIEW can break after the search_path change. We might want to either pre-compile these queries somehow or retain the search path for the later resolution.
> 
> Yes, that is a good point. One possible solution here would be to store the search path with the view, and then on the binder level switch the active search path around. Not super crucial for an initial pass.

Agreed. Leaving it as is.

Okay, the "did you mean" suggestion is back with the suggested improvement.
PTAL?

Node.js 15 Windows error is:

> npm ERR! network request to https://registry.npmjs.org/aws-sdk failed, reason: connect ETIMEDOUT 104.16.23.35:443

So probably a flake.
Thanks for the review again Mark! Updated the code. Please take a look?
Thanks for the changes! Looks good now. Will merge after the tests pass.

issue_context.title: Set default schema that is used at runtime
comments:
Hi @Mytherin,

can you please guide about the changes. Will be happy to pick this up.

Thanks for the offer :)

Apologies for the late reply, I have been a bit busy. Here are the changes required as I see them:

What needs to happen for this change is that anytime the DEFAULT_SCHEMA is bound, we instead use the default schema that is specified by the user. The default schema is client-dependent, and should reset every session, so we can store this in the `ClientContext` as a simple string. It should have the default `DEFAULT_SCHEMA` as default value (which is "main" currently).

We then need to support actually changing this variable. An easy way of doing that for now would be through the `PRAGMA` statement, e.g. `PRAGMA default_schema='s1'`. This case should be handled in `physical_pragma.cpp`.

The variable then needs to be used in the actual binding. This all happens in `catalog.cpp`. Anytime we encounter `DEFAULT_SCHEMA` there, we need to switch this to use the variable located in the client context. Note that we should also do this for create statements. For example, if you do `CREATE TABLE integers(i INTEGER);`, the actual table created should be in the default schema.

I believe those are all the changes required, at least as I see it right now.

review_comments: Explicit `StringUtil::Lower` should not be required here as the catalog uses case insensitive lookups.
